# markdown-s2 — Safe Markdown → HTML renderer (tier S2) ## Module: `src/markdown.js` (ES module) - `export function render(markdown: string, { headingIds = false } = {}): string` → HTML. - `export function toc(markdown: string): Array<{ level: number, text: string, slug: string }>` — every ATX/setext heading in document order; `text` is the heading's plain text (inline markup removed). - `export function slugify(text: string, seen?: Map)` — GitHub-style slug: lower-case; remove every character that is not a letter, digit, space, `-` or `_`; spaces → `-`. When a `Map` of previously seen slugs is passed, repeated slugs get `-1`, `-2`, … suffixes. `toc` and `headingIds` use one map per document. ## Output conventions Follow CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by the reference implementation commonmark.js) plus GFM tables and strikethrough, except where this spec says otherwise. Insignificant whitespace between block-level tags is not significant to the tests; `
`/`

`, ``/`` are equivalent; table alignment may be expressed as `align="left"` or `style="text-align:left"`. Required features: - ATX headings `#`…`######` (closing `#`s stripped), setext headings (`===`, `---`). With `headingIds: true`, headings get `id=""`: `

My title

`. - Paragraphs; soft line breaks preserved as `\n`; hard breaks via two trailing spaces or a trailing backslash → `
`. - Emphasis/strong with `*` and `_` (CommonMark rules incl. no intraword `_` emphasis), `***x***` → `x`; GFM `~~strike~~` → ``. - Code spans (multi-backtick delimiters, one leading/trailing space stripped when both present). - Fenced code blocks (``` and ~~~, info string → `class="language-"`) and indented code blocks. - Blockquotes (nested, with lazy continuation lines), thematic breaks (`---`, `***`, `___`). - Bullet lists (`-`, `*`, `+`) and ordered lists (`1.` / `1)`, `start` attribute when not 1), nesting by indentation, tight vs loose lists (`

  • ` when loose). - Inline links `[t](url "title")`, images `![alt](src "title")`, reference links `[t][ref]`, `[ref]` with definitions `[ref]: url "title"` (case-insensitive labels), autolinks `` and `<>` (→ `mailto:`). - Backslash escapes; HTML-escape `& < > "` in text, attributes and code. - GFM pipe tables with header row, delimiter row, optional alignment (`:--`, `:-:`, `--:`), inline markup in cells, `\|` escapes. ## Safety (deliberate deviation from CommonMark) - Raw HTML (block and inline) is NOT passed through: it is rendered as escaped text, e.g. `` → `

    <script>x</script>

content.text:
I wrote the renderer from scratch in `src/markdown.js`, with the CLI in `src/cli.js`. `node --test` passes: 21 tests, the public smoke tests plus 19 of mine in `tests/impl.test.js`.

My checks covered most SPEC features. I also ran the CLI on a sample file with `--ids` and on stdin with `--toc`, and both gave the expected output. I did not run a CommonMark spec conformance suite, so edge cases beyond my own tests are unchecked.

- **Retrieval decision:** I judged writing it myself cheaper than retrieving. Adapting commonmark.js would have meant converting it to ESM and then patching in the spec's deviations (no raw HTML, URL scheme filtering, tables). Nothing was vendored, so `PROVENANCE.json` stays `[]` and there is no `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- **Approach:** the block and inline parsers follow the CommonMark algorithms, including tab handling and tight vs loose lists.
- **Raw HTML:** it is never passed through. Block-level HTML such as `<div>` is parsed as an ordinary paragraph, so Markdown inside it is still processed and the tags come out escaped.
- **Limited entity table:** named HTML entities are supported only from a short built-in table of about 50. An unrecognised named entity stays as literal text, where commonmark.js would decode it. Numeric entities are fully handled.
- **Repeated heading slugs:** the third `a` gets `a-2`, and so on. A heading that literally slugs to `a-1` is not checked against these generated suffixes.
